original_question: For each odd degree d = 2m + 1 >= 5, does there exist a maximizing plane curve C_{2m+1} having only simple singularities of type A, D, E and satisfying tau(C) = 3m^2 + 1?
target_in_paper: Section 7, Question 7.5, read together with Definition 7.3 and Proposition 7.4. ([imar.ro](https://imar.ro/journals/Revue_Mathematique/pdfs/2024/2/4.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper's intended target very closely: it asks for existence in every odd degree d = 2m + 1 ≥ 5, uses the paper's odd-degree maximizing condition τ(C) = 3m^2 + 1, and restricts to simple singularities of type A, D, E. ([imar.ro](https://imar.ro/journals/Revue_Mathematique/pdfs/2024/2/4.pdf))
missing_details: The ambient setting should be explicit: throughout the paper one works with reduced projective plane curves C : f = 0 in ℙ^2 over ℂ, with f a reduced homogeneous polynomial in S = ℂ[x, y, z]. ([imar.ro](https://imar.ro/journals/Revue_Mathematique/pdfs/2024/2/4.pdf))

The word "maximizing" is a defined term here, not just an informal adjective: in odd degree d = 2m + 1 ≥ 5 it means exactly a reduced curve in ℙ^2 with only A, D, E singularities and total Tjurina number τ(C) = 3m^2 + 1. ([imar.ro](https://imar.ro/journals/Revue_Mathematique/pdfs/2024/2/4.pdf))

The quantifier should be stated as 'for every integer m ≥ 2' (equivalently, for every odd degree d = 2m + 1 ≥ 5). The paper phrases the official problem as existence 'in any degree d = 2m + 1 ≥ 5'. ([imar.ro](https://imar.ro/journals/Revue_Mathematique/pdfs/2024/2/4.pdf))

To be stand-alone, τ(C) should be identified as the total Tjurina number, i.e. the sum of the local Tjurina numbers of the singularities of C. ([imar.ro](https://imar.ro/journals/Revue_Mathematique/pdfs/2024/2/4.pdf))

The draft leaves implicit the nearby structural consequence supplied by Proposition 7.4: any such odd-degree maximizing curve would necessarily satisfy r = mdr(f) = m − 1, and equality there is exactly the free case. ([imar.ro](https://imar.ro/journals/Revue_Mathematique/pdfs/2024/2/4.pdf))

There is no separate nilpotency or formal-power-series hypothesis in this problem; the paper's relevant hidden restriction is reducedness of the homogeneous defining equation. ([imar.ro](https://imar.ro/journals/Revue_Mathematique/pdfs/2024/2/4.pdf))
refined_question: For every integer m ≥ 2, does there exist a maximizing curve C_{2m+1}, meaning a reduced projective plane curve C = V(f) ⊂ ℙ^2 over ℂ defined by a reduced homogeneous polynomial f ∈ ℂ[x, y, z] of degree d = 2m + 1, whose singularities are all simple of type A, D, E and whose total Tjurina number is τ(C) = 3m^2 + 1? ([imar.ro](https://imar.ro/journals/Revue_Mathematique/pdfs/2024/2/4.pdf))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalent via Proposition 7.4 together with Corollary 2.6 (and Theorem 2.2 for the exponent statement): for every integer m ≥ 2, does there exist a reduced free curve C = V(f) ⊂ ℙ^2 over ℂ of degree 2m + 1 with only A, D, E singularities and mdr(f) = m − 1, equivalently with free exponents (m − 1, m + 1)? ([imar.ro](https://imar.ro/journals/Revue_Mathematique/pdfs/2024/2/4.pdf))
justification: The nearest official formulation is the specific open existence problem in Section 7, not a broader neighboring question. Definition 7.3 supplies the exact odd-degree meaning of 'maximizing', Proposition 7.4 explains why 3m^2 + 1 is the relevant extremal Tjurina value and why attaining it forces the curve into the free case r = m − 1, and Question 7.5 then asks precisely whether such maximizing curves exist in every odd degree. The introduction also says that, at the time of this paper, odd-degree examples with these properties were known only up to degree 9. ([imar.ro](https://imar.ro/journals/Revue_Mathematique/pdfs/2024/2/4.pdf))
